why: The one live stability bug, now located (2026-11-01): every post-mortem since 10-25 is a hang inside the PIO-USB host's timer interrupt, about one every 3 h, with the USB audio DAC stream the first suspect. A soak with usb_audio = off is cheap and splits the question; it runs on one board while features are built on the other.

The quick MIDI win (user, 2026-11-01), chosen over the bit-banger path: one emulated chip, the MIDI Pak's 6850 at $FF6E, covers Lyra, UltiMusE III and CoCo MIDI Pro, needs no fine bit timing, and the native USB-C port is already plugged into the Mac, so a DAW hears the CoCo with no extra hardware. The host-port half the standard needs follows as PIZERO-305.

Retires the biggest unknown in the plan: what Disk BASIC's sector writes mean. A hardware trace with the existing pizero_fdctrace env, written up as the spec PIZERO-292 implements; cheap, and best done before any write code.
The first thing users see: a host directory in a drive, read by an unmodified Disk BASIC. Needs PIZERO-289; mountable by editing drives.txt on the Mac until PIZERO-293 adds it on the board.
Makes directory drives the everyday storage: SAVE, KILL and RENAME land as host files with no disk full. Needs PIZERO-290 and the write spec from PIZERO-291.

The AY chips are in (PIZERO-149) and proven with our own programs; one real piece of software playing through them is what makes the feature real for users. Lyra 1.2 for the Symphony-12 is the likeliest to run today; the Sierra games wait on PSRAM.

Small, everyday experience win with nothing blocking it: whole-file writes exist, so booting back into the last game is mostly a precedence rule against autorun. A good change of pace between CoCo 3 stages.
Hot-plug: every software path is disproved, but one cheap test is left (unplug and replug through the simple hub). If it works the answer is 'use a hub' and the issue closes.

Other people's screens, which the kits rest on. Since PIZERO-232 changed the HDMI audio delivery, two screens that garbled sound now play it cleanly; the dev monitor and the upstairs Samsung still need a recheck (PIZERO-233). One LCD remains odd on both picture and sound (PIZERO-120, PIZERO-234), and a Raspberry Pi at 640x480p60 on it would tell monitor from signal. Opportunistic: whenever a screen is to hand.
